CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic fluid
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing with Turner syndrome indication

TESTS PERFORMED
1. Rapid aneuploidy detection by quantitative fluorescence PCR (QF-PCR)
2. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for sex chromosomes
3. G-banded chromosome analysis (karyotype)

RESULTS

RAPID PCR (Completed [redacted date])
QF-PCR analysis of STR markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y
Result: Single X chromosome signal detected. No Y chromosome material identified.

FISH ANALYSIS (Completed [redacted date])
Probes: CEP X (DXZ1) and CEP Y (DYZ3)
Result: nuc ish (DXZ1x1)
One X chromosome signal in 200/200 interphase nuclei examined

KARYOTYPE ANALYSIS
Method: G-banded analysis at 400-550 band resolution
Cells analyzed: 20 metaphases from 3 independent cultures
Result: 45,X

INTERPRETATION
Abnormal female karyotype with single X chromosome in all examined cells, consistent with Turner syndrome. No evidence of mosaicism detected in this analysis.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
This karyotype confirms the diagnosis of Turner syndrome (monosomy X). Turner syndrome is associated with short stature, ovarian dysgenesis, and potential congenital anomalies including cardiac defects (particularly left-sided lesions), renal anomalies, and lymphedema. Intelligence is typically normal, though specific learning difficulties may occur.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. If pregnancy terminates: Please collect cord blood (lithium heparin tube) and fetal tissue (sterile container) to confirm this finding
2. Detailed fetal ultrasound evaluation for associated anomalies if pregnancy continues
3. Prenatal diagnosis is available for future pregnancies
4. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss implications and recurrence risks

PATIENT EDUCATION MATERIALS
Information sheets on Turner syndrome are available through our genetic counseling service. Please contact [redacted phone] to schedule an appointment.

This analysis has a detection limit of approximately 10% for mosaicism. Lower levels of mosaicism may not be detected.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
